MMM.rationale: MMM is extremely unattractive at current levels. The business exhibits severe earnings deterioration: GAAP EPS collapsed 39.7% YoY to $1.23 in Q1 2026, net margin compressed from 18.8% to 10.9%, and total equity eroded 26.8% to $3.31B, producing a 9.7x liabilities-to-equity ratio. The market has responded by expanding the PE from ~18x to ~30x, creating a negative equity risk premium (3.4% earnings yield vs 4.54% 10Y Treasury). The qualitative report's 'execution improving' narrative is materially propped up by PIT-leaked Q2 2026 data (Morningstar Jul 21) that is not available as of the decision date. Stripping that data, the legitimate pre-decision evidence shows adjusted EPS of $2.14 vs GAAP $1.23 — a $0.91 quality-of-earnings gap that the qual report does not adequately flag. The adjusted beat vs consensus ($2.14 vs $1.99) is the sole positive datapoint, but it is overwhelmed by GAAP deterioration, balance-sheet erosion, and a 30x multiple on declining earnings. Tariff exposure of up to $850M annually and ongoing PFAS/earplug litigation liabilities add further downside risk. A mean reversion to the historical 18-20x PE on the current $1.23 quarterly EPS run-rate implies ~35-40% downside. The Q2 earnings call on July 21 is a potential catalyst but could easily disappoint given the GAAP-adjusted spread and tariff headwinds.
